question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
**Yes.** In the latest CPI data (August 2026), electricity prices were up **13.2%** year on year, against **4.0%** for all groups CPI.

Electricity has been well ahead of headline inflation for most of the past year:

- **Electricity:** 37.0% (Feb 2026), 25.4% (Mar), 22.5% (Apr), 21.1% (May), 22.4% (Jun), 6.1% (Jul), 13.2% (Aug)
- **All groups:** 3.7% (Feb 2026), 4.6% (Mar), 4.2% (Apr), 4.0% (May), 3.8% (Jun), 3.5% (Jul), 4.0% (Aug)

The gap peaked in early 2026, when electricity was running at roughly 8 to 10 times the headline rate. It has narrowed since then. The July 2026 electricity reading dropped sharply to 6.1%, then rebounded to 13.2% in August, so the monthly pattern is volatile.

The 2024–25 electricity figures are hard to read as a trend. They show deep negative annual rates (about -36% in October 2024) followed by a sharp jump from July 2025, which looks like the effect of government energy bill rebates being added and then removed. Those base effects also affect the current year-on-year numbers, so I'd treat the size of the gap with some caution. The data here doesn't tell me the exact causes of the July 2026 dip and August rebound.
